items.abstract: <jats:p>Significant wave height (SWH) forecasting plays an essential role in marine renewable energy utilization, offshore engineering operations, navigation safety, and extreme-sea-state warnings. However, SWH evolution is governed by the nonlinear interactions among local wind forcing, remote swell propagation, oceanographic conditions, and extreme weather systems, resulting in strong non-stationarity, multi-scale oscillations, and abrupt fluctuations. These characteristics make accurate multi-step forecasting particularly challenging, as existing data-driven models often suffer from insufficient frequency representation, unstable decomposition performance, and error accumulation over long prediction horizons. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel hybrid forecasting framework, termed VMD-IMDE-BiMambawave, which integrates adaptive signal decomposition, evolutionary parameter optimization, and bidirectional selective state-space modeling. First, variational mode decomposition (VMD) is introduced to separate the original SWH sequence into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) with different frequency characteristics, thereby reducing the complexity caused by nonlinear and non-stationary fluctuations. Considering that the decomposition quality of VMD is highly sensitive to manually selected parameters, an island migration differential evolution (IMDE) algorithm is developed to automatically optimize the mode number and penalty factor according to forecasting performance. The proposed IMDE incorporates island-based parallel evolution, Gaussian process surrogate-assisted evaluation, dynamic elite migration, and stagnation restart strategies to improve optimization efficiency and robustness. items.abstract: <jats:p>As substation equipment continues to evolve toward higher voltage levels, larger capacities, and more complex operating conditions, voiceprint signals exhibit greater sensitivity and observability during the early stages of faults. However, traditional modeling approaches still suffer from limitations in capturing long-range temporal dependencies, suppressing noise interference, and adapting to unlabeled data. To address these issues, a state space model-based Mamba self-supervised voiceprint framework, termed MSANet, is proposed. A bidirectional state space scanning mechanism is introduced into the network architecture to avoid the high computational complexity of attention mechanisms while simultaneously preserving both global contextual correlations and local detail representations of voiceprint signals. In addition, a spectrum block masking-based self-supervised learning strategy is incorporated, enabling the model to extract stable time–frequency structural features even under unlabeled or limited labeled samples. Experimental results demonstrate that MSANet achieves high accuracy in voiceprint-related tasks. Furthermore, the lightweight version of the model maintains competitive performance while significantly reducing computational and storage overhead, indicating its feasibility for deployment on edge devices in resource-constrained scenarios such as substation environments. The proposed method provides a potential methodological basis for enhancing fault-related voiceprint feature extraction, representation learning, and future practical engineering deployment.</jats:p>
title: Self-Supervised Bidirectional State Space Modeling for Voiceprint Feature Representation and Recognition
